items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the navigation law, in relation to personal watercraft; and to repeal certain provisions of such law relating thereto
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S7359

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the navigation law, in relation to personal
watercraft; and to repeal certain provisions of such law relating
thereto


 PURPOSE OF THE BILL :

This bill would update state laws applicable to the operation of
personal watercraft to conform to federal laws and industry safety
recommendations.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1 of the bill would repeal the definition of "specialty
prop-craft" in Navigation Law (NL) § 2(31); replace the definition of
"personal watercraft" in NL § 2(30) with a new definition of that term
and number it NL § 2(31); and add a definition of "livery."

Section 2 of the bill would delete references to "specialty
prop-craft" in NL § 49(1-a), and delete an expired transition
provision related to the previously-enacted statutory increase in the
permissible age at which a personal watercraft may be operated.

Section 3 of the bill would amend NL § 71-d(2) to correct an
inconsistency in the penalty provision by making a violation of
section 71-d punishable as set forth in section 73-c of the Navigation
Law.

Section 4 of the bill would amend NL § 73-a to delete references to
"specialty propcraft;" update the equipment required to be on a
personal watercraft; add a new provision prohibiting passengers on
personal watercraft from sitting in front of the operator and
requiring that passengers be of sufficient height to sit securely on
the personal watercraft; increase the minimum age at which a person
can rent a personal watercraft from sixteen to eighteen; require
livery personnel to have completed a boating safety course if they are
responsible for demonstrating personal watercraft operation and safety
to patrons; and require the livery to provide patrons with all
required safety and other equipment and explain the use of the
equipment.

Section 5 of the bill would provide that the bill would take effect 30
days after it becomes law; provided that NL § 73-a(2)(g) and (h), as
added by section 4 of the bill, would take effect January 1, 2011; and
provided further that the amendments to NL § 73-a(2)(f) would be
deemed repealed when that paragraph expires.

 EXISTING LAW :

NL § 2 provides definitions for "personal watercraft" and "specialty
prop-craft," but does not provide a definition for "livery."
Throughout the Navigation Law, the term "specialty propcraft" is used
in addition to the term "personal watercraft."

NL § 73-a(1)(c) and (d) require certain types of equipment to be
located on personal watercraft.

NL § 73-a(2)(a) allows liveries to rent personal watercraft to those
16 years of age and older and requires liveries to explain and
demonstrate safe operation of the personal watercraft.  There is no
requirement that liveries or their agent hold a boating safety
certificate.
 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This is a new proposal.

 STATEMENT IN SUPPORT :

A personal watercraft is a small vessel operated by a person sitting,
standing or kneeling on the boat, or being towed behind it, and that
is propelled by a water jet pump or other mechanical power. The
personal watercraft (PWC) concept originated in the 1960s, and New
York added the regulation of PWC to the Navigation Law in 1990 as
their use became more prevalent. As the industry has made changes to
PWC, and as federal law has adapted, the State law should be updated
accordingly. This bill would update State law to comport with federal
law, industry safety recommendations and common terminology; and would
correct inconsistencies in the current law.

The bill would delete the references to "specialty prop-craft" because
such vessels are largely obsolete. However, in the event such vessels
reemerge in the marketplace, the bill would ensure that the new
definition of "personal watercraft" would apply to those vessels
considered specialty prop-craft so that they are properly regulated as
vessels.

The bill would delete an obsolete requirement that PWC include at
least two ventilators fitted with cowls. This requirement is
unnecessary because engines of PWC, unlike traditional motorized
vessels, are open to the air and use a natural ventilation system.
Federal law now requires a B-1 sized United States Coast Guard
approved fire extinguisher and a specific type of distress flag.
Accordingly, this bill Could amended NL § 73-a to comport with federal
law.

In response to horrific accidents that have severely and fatality
injured passengers, mainly children, the Personal Watercraft Industry
Association (PWIA) has recommended that passengers not ride in front
of operators and that passengers be of sufficient size to properly sit
on PWC. Consistent with these common sense recommendations, this bill
would make those industry safety recommendations the law in New York.

Customers who rent PWC from liveries are not required to take a
boating safety course.  To ensure that such persons receive proper
instruction, the bill would require livery personnel to complete a
boating safety course if they are responsible for explaining to the
customer how to safely operate the PWC. The bill would further require
the livery to fully outfit the PWC with all required equipment in
serviceable condition and to explain to the person renting the PWC how
and when to use the safety equipment. These provisions would help
ensure the safe operation of PWC rented from a livery.

 BUDGET IMPLICATIONS :

None.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
The bill would take effect 30 days after it becomes law; provided that
NL § 73-a(2)(g) and (f), as added by section 4 of the bill, would take
effect January 1, 2011; and provided further that the amendments to NL
§ 73-a(2)(f) would be deemed repealed when that paragraph expires
(currently January 1, 2012).
